label: 死亡与第二周目
before: The player unlocks and enters the moonlight tower for the first time.
beat: Low fallen-candle point of view in the referenced pipe-organ tower. A brass candlestick lies on cold stone, the just-extinguished wick sends a thin thread of smoke toward blood-red moonlight from the tall window. The organ is distant and forbidding; a swirling dark red mist folds the edges of the room, expressing sudden death and the night resetting. No body or face, no gore. Rich red-black and cold silver, a legible candle silhouette.
after: The player awakens in the hall; the fireplace is out and the armor has changed position.

label: 真相与第三周目
before: Four burnt letter fragments have finally been assembled and read.
beat: A detailed close view of FOUR torn aged letter fragments neatly fitted into ONE complete letter on an antique wooden desk. Matching charred edges remain visible. Beside it a sealed inkpot and one unlit candle, snow and cold moonlight outside a soft-focus gothic window. An understated warm gold thread of light follows the repaired seams, conveying forgiveness and the long-awaited reply. No readable words, just small indistinct handwriting marks, no hands or people.
after: The organ calls from the tower; the third loop begins, now as a wait for a reply rather than a hunt.

label: 追捕失败结局
before: The player fails a pursuit or the keepsake protection expires.
beat: The last candle has rolled onto the foreground floor of a narrow gothic corridor; its wick is dark and its wax runs cold. The far heavy wooden door is CLOSED, a severe blood-red shaft of moonlight cuts across the stone, blue-black mist crowds the path. A broken brass candlestick and a small scatter of glass catch the last red reflection. The escape route feels definitively lost, static and silent. No pursuer, face, eyes, hands, human form, death body or gore.
after: Wrong Ending remains on screen until the player explicitly restarts or returns to the ensemble.

label: 密室追逐
before: Adrian begins pursuing the player inside the castle.
beat: An urgent first-person view down a LONG gothic corridor with ribbed arches and crooked red curtains, a partly OPEN door at the far end revealing a slim blue escape light. A candle burns on a bracket halfway down the wall, red mist and sharp diagonal moonlight behind the viewer. The foreground path is clear and open, desperate but escapable, unlike the blocked Wrong Ending. Fine architectural detail, a slight sense of motion only in peripheral mist. No hand, figure, silhouette, face, eyes or gore.
after: The player performs a hold, rhythm or tapping gesture to escape.

label: 第一乐章·悲怆
before: The first movement of the requiem is played; Adrian cannot touch the soul fragment.
beat: The referenced pipe-organ tower in a quiet, grieving early dawn. A SINGLE delicate BLUE soul-light ribbon settles on the EMPTY organ bench and fades into a tiny warm glow; the organ score is still, a single tear-like bead of light rests on a key, the moon is paling and only a thin silver-peach line of dawn touches the window sill. Restrained sorrow and release, predominantly cool blue, low warm light. No human, figure, face, humanoid ghost or silhouette.
after: The first sunrise begins to enter the room and the player may explore after dawn.

label: 第二乐章·柔情
before: The second movement is played; the two spirits recognize and forgive each other.
beat: The same pipe-organ tower, a closer intimate composition of antique keys and completed score. Exactly TWO thin translucent soul-light ribbons, one blue and one warm gold, gently intertwine above the keys like a quiet duet, meeting without taking human shape. Soft peach sunrise reflects in polished wood, tiny dust motes hang still, the gothic window and organ pipes retain the reference architecture. Tender, calm, warm, a reunion expressed through two lights. No person, face, outline, hands or humanoid ghost.
after: Both soul lights dissolve into the dawn together.

label: 第三乐章·永别
before: The final movement is completed with the recovered memories and keepsakes.
beat: A grand wide view of the referenced organ tower as a brilliant BLUE AND GOLD COLUMN of soul light rises from the completed score, scattering luminous music-like particles into the first powerful golden sunrise through the gothic window. Three score pages lift slightly on the organ stand; a ring and stopped pocket watch rest safely at the keyboard edge. Triumphant, bittersweet, solemn release, the strongest dawn and brightest contrast of the three endings. No human form, person, face, arm, silhouette or ghost body.
after: The two spirits see their first sunrise together; the castle opens for peaceful exploration.

label: 安魂曲补全
before: The player brings the quill to the damaged requiem and restores the missing movements.
beat: A crisp still life on the antique pipe-organ music stand: THREE complete aged score pages with coherent small staves and musical marks, a feather quill resting on a dark inkpot beside them, a ring and closed pocket watch lower on the wooden ledge, gentle gold light tracing the newly repaired paper edges. The tower pipes are softly visible behind, cool moonlight balanced with one warm candle. No legible text or page headings; no hand, face or person.
after: The repaired requiem can now be played to determine the final movement ending.
